content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.3) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (sentiment < -0.3) — model ignores downside risk and fails to adjust downward.
- Model exhibits lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns from negative to positive, forecast lags 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility and fails to smoothly revert to historical mean in 10–15 day horizons.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves — model forecasts peak too high and then underestimates subsequent pullback.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is positive, model tends to overfit upward momentum; when negative, it underfits downward pressure.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in early periods (e.g., 2025-10-07 to 10-13) — model overestimates upward trend in bullish sentiment windows.
